jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
Description:
**Department:** Development

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Position:** Director of Development

**Employment Type:** Full\-time, exempt, salaried and benefited

**Agency Description:** We provide affordable, bilingual, and accessible mental health services for people of all ages living in Napa County. Our vision is to create a community of enduring strength by equipping children, youth, adults, and seniors with the tools they need to live emotionally healthy and stable lives through programs ranging from prevention to mental health treatment.

**Position Summary:** The Development Director (DD) leads and oversees all aspects of the agency’s philanthropic and communications activities. Working closely with the Executive Director, Executive Leadership team, Board of Directors, and Development staff, the DD drives dynamic development, builds donor relationships, and marketing strategies that meet and exceed the agency’s goals.


**Duties and Responsibilities**


Leadership \& Strategy

* Works closely with Executive Director, Leadership Team, and Board Development Committee to create and implement annual and long\-term development and marketing strategies that help meet and exceed the agency’s revenue, service delivery, and community engagement goals.
* Leads Board Development/Stewardship Committee, strategically leveraging its membership to support community engagement and fundraising initiatives
* Strategically supports Marketing Committee
* Develop and monitor annual Development revenue targets and expense budget with an eye toward maximizing fundraising efficiency and ROI on expenses.


Gifts and Philanthropy

* Develop and cultivate donor relationships as well as solicit funds.
* Leads Mentis giving program, working closely with ED, Board, and Development committee to ensure regular (at least quarterly) engagement with all donors.
* Builds, sustains, and models a culture of stewardship, emphasizing long\-term relationship\-building over continual asking.
* Manages a personal portfolio of donors in conjunction with ED as well as supports ED with ongoing major donor engagement.
* Works with ED, Board, and Development committee to continually identify and cultivate potential new major donors.


Events and Fundraising

* Oversee execution of Mentis’ community engagement events, including Jeffersonian Dinner series, Blue Skies Ahead reception, Mental Health Awareness Month event, Donor breakfast, and potential other events, and annual fundraising campaigns, including end\-of\-year giving, monthly giving, Mental Health Awareness Month, Suicide Prevention Month, and others throughout the year.
* Support the Development Team in project\-managing all events and fundraising campaigns, including workplan tracking, budget monitoring, and supervising team tasks.
* Oversee messaging, guest experience and strategy, ensuring that all events and campaigns are executed with high fidelity to the Mentis brand and agency values.


Institutional Funding

* Work with Grant management consultant (who will write larger grants) and other directors on smaller/local grants, to manage annual grants pipeline, ensuring that all proposal and reporting deadlines are met and that continual prospect research identifies new funding opportunities.
* Coordinate with program staff where needed to gather program data and other content for grant proposals and reports.


Communications \& Marketing

* Work with the Development Team to develop an engaging annual communications strategy and plan that meets the agency’s community engagement and fundraising goals.
* Support Development Team in creating and publishing engaging materials for a variety of audiences—including press releases, columns, media pitches, e\-blasts, advertisements, radio features, event promotion materials, impact reports, and more.
* Serve as Mentis spokesperson along with other directors and board members, representing the agency in public through presentations, media interviews, and local event attendance.


Administration

* Develop and monitor annual development budget in conjunction with ED and Finance Director.
* Work with Development Team to analyze monthly reports on fundraising revenue and progress toward goals.


Supervision

* Provide effective and supportive supervision for Development Team.
* Encourage and provide professional growth opportunities.
* Monitor performance and provide guidance, support, and oversight where needed.


Other Duties as Assigned

Compensation is based on a variety of factors, including education, experience, and skill set.

Earn up to 12 vacation days per year

jobs.title: Vice President of Development
jobs.description:
***“Every person deserves compassion, dignity, and the safety of a place to call home.”***
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*Homelessness is the largest social and public health crisis in California. Illumination Health \+ Home is a growing non\-profit organization dedicated towards disrupting the cycle of homelessness by providing targeted, interdisciplinary services in our recuperative care centers, emergency shelters, housing services and children's and family programs. IH\+H currently has 13\+ facilities with 22\+ micro\-communities scattered across Orange County, Los Angeles County and the Inland Empire.*

**The Opportunity**


We are seeking a strategic, hands\-on Vice President of Development to lead and grow our philanthropic revenue while building a high\-performing, mission\-driven team. Reporting to the CEO and serving on the executive leadership team, you will shape and execute a multi\-year fundraising strategy spanning major gifts, individual giving, corporate and foundation partnerships, special events, Board engagement, and campaign development.


This is a leadership role for a fundraiser who loves both the work and the people. You will set strategy and lead a team, while personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors and philanthropic partners.  

  

The pay range for this position is **$155,000 \- $175,000 annually**, depending on experience.  

  

**What you'll do**


Fundraising Strategy \& Revenue Growth* Develop and execute a three\-year comprehensive fundraising strategy aligned with organizational priorities, with annual goals by revenue stream and quarterly revenue, pipeline, and activity targets.
* Maintain a fundraising pipeline sufficient to support 2–3 times the annual major\-gift and institutional goals, and identify opportunities to diversify revenue and grow unrestricted support.
* Monitor performance and provide the CEO and Board with regular reports on revenue, pipeline, projections, and progress, partnering with Finance on accurate forecasts.

  

Major Gifts \& Individual Philanthropy

* Build and personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors, developing individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.
* Personally lead or participate in five\-, six\-, and seven\-figure solicitations, and grow the number and value of major gifts.
* Develop compelling cases for support, and partner with the CEO and Board to identify and engage high\-capacity individuals and community influencers.
* Build and deepen relationships with corporations, foundations, and institutional partners, moving funders from transactional grants toward strategic, multi\-year partnerships.

  

Corporate, Foundation \& Board Engagement

* Build and deepen relationships with corporations, foundations, and institutional partners, moving funders from transactional grants toward strategic, multi\-year partnerships.
* Partner with the CEO and Board to maximize their effectiveness as ambassadors and fundraisers, setting clear annual engagement expectations and providing tools, coaching, and meeting preparation.
* Create opportunities for Board members to leverage their networks to expand the donor base.

  

Donor Stewardship \& Campaigns

* Design and lead a comprehensive stewardship strategy, with a goal of increasing donor retention by at least 5% in the first year.
* Drive donor upgrades, recurring and multi\-year giving, and re\-engagement of lapsed donors, ensuring donors receive timely, meaningful communication about their impact.
* Assess organizational readiness for future capital and transformational campaigns, completing a campaign readiness assessment within the first six months.

  

Team Leadership \& Operations

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of seven, setting clear goals and expectations and fostering a culture that is collaborative, supportive, accountable, and donor\-centered.
* Lead with kindness, humility, professionalism, and respect while maintaining high standards, and encourage collaboration across Finance, Programs, Marketing, and Executive Leadership.
* Ensure the CRM is fully utilized for fundraising management, with standardized dashboards, reliable monthly and quarterly forecasting, and accurate reporting in partnership with Finance.

 **What you'll bring**

* Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.
* 8–10\+ years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising experience, including leading development functions and managing fundraising professionals.
* Demonstrated success securing major gifts, ideally at the five\-, six\-, and seven\-figure levels.
* Proven ability to build fundraising strategies that produce measurable revenue growth.
* Experience across major gifts, individual giving, corporate and foundation relations, events, stewardship, and campaign planning.
* Skilled at partnering with CEOs, Boards, major donors, and community leaders.
* Experience with CRM systems, pipeline development, forecasting, and metrics\-driven management.
* Strong financial acumen and excellent communication and relationship\-building skills.
* Experience in healthcare, homelessness, housing, or human services preferred.
* Meaningful connections within Orange County and/or Southern California a plus.

 **Who you are**  

  

You are an entrepreneurial, relationship\-oriented fundraising leader who pairs a strong track record of results with genuine care for people. You lead with kindness, humility, and accountability, you are comfortable rolling up your sleeves alongside your team, and you bring energy, creativity, and a genuine commitment to our mission.

 **Benefits**

* Medical Insurance funded up to 91% by Illumination Foundation (Kaiser and Blue Shield), depending on the plan
* Dental and Vision Insurance
* Life, AD\&D and LTD Insurance funded 100% by Illumination Foundation
* Employee Assistance Program
* Professional Development Reimbursement
*

jobs.title: Chief Philanthropy Officer - Providence Saint Joseph Burbank
jobs.description:
**Description**

**Calling All Esteemed Leaders!** Are you an experienced philanthropy leader with a passion for major and transformational giving, board engagement, and advancing mission\-driven healthcare? Do you thrive at the intersection of strategic leadership, donor engagement, and organizational impact? If so, we invite you to explore this opportunity with Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center.


**The Role**

The Chief Philanthropy Officer (CPO) for Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center serves as a key leadership team member and an active participant in making strategic decisions affecting the Foundation. In partnership with the Chief Philanthropy and Health Equity Officer, South Division, this position is responsible for fundraising and development of major gift activities related to the medical center's key Institutes, service lines, campuses, and relevant medical programs.


The CPO will also work closely with the Chief Executive, Foundation Board of Directors, Senior Director of Philanthropy, Campaigns and Senior Director of Philanthropy, Donor Relations. The CPO will mentor and coach the philanthropy officers (development officers) and respective support staff on the major gifts team to identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major gift donors, and identify opportunities to strengthen, leverage and engage the organization's constituents and volunteers in meaningful ways.


The CPO leads a multi\-year effort to substantially grow the Foundation's annual philanthropic support. As part of the Foundation's leadership team, the CPO shall assist with developing a system\-wide philanthropy vision and strategy aligned with the Foundation's strategic goals and priorities. The CPO shall assist in planning, developing, organizing, implementing, directing, and evaluating all the Foundation's major gift activities to ensure all short and long\-term objectives are fully achieved.


The CPO develops new and more diverse sources of philanthropic support by emphasizing major gifts and seven figure\+ transformational gifts in order to generate an ROI that justifies a growing investment of resources in the Foundation's fundraising capacity. The CPO drives and implements a culture of philanthropy throughout Mission Hospital, and works closely with Institute leadership, physician leaders and other caregivers to improve and expand the Foundation's grateful patient fundraising programs.


At all times, the CPO partners with Foundation leadership to identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit, and steward key individuals, foundations, corporations and others. The CPO manages a portfolio of approximately 50 major/principal gift\-level prospects and donors and is responsible for achieving a personal philanthropic revenue goal each year.

* Functions as a visionary strategic thinker setting the strategic and annual operating plan to achieve the goals of the Foundation.
* Serves as a member of the Executive Leadership Team. Works collaboratively with the senior leadership team and with medical staff leaders to identify organizational priorities, including clinical program development and capital needs.

* Maintains professional contact with community organizations, other institutions, associations and organizations that affect hospital development programs.
* Maintains open communication with other foundation executives and staff within Providence, ensuring the exchange of ideas and information that would help promote success in all foundations.
* Works effectively with the Foundation Board of Directors in their responsibilities as the fundraising arm of the hospital. Develops an effective structure for the Board; ensures that the Board is able to achieve its goals and priorities, consistent with the philanthropic strategic plan.
* Assists the Board in creation and implementation of policies and procedures that will ensure utilization of the most effective, economical and ethical methods of fundraising.
* Organizes the Board for maximum efficiency and ensures that Foundation Board Members' time and talents are well\-utilized to make optimal philanthropic impact. Recruits new Board Members as needed.
* Responsible for the development of principal and major gift prospects for the medical center and for maintaining and building relationships with existing donors.
* Confers with the appropriate hospital leadership to identify key organizational needs and develops presentations, case statements and compelling stories for support from prospective donors. Works in close collaboration with the marketing department, to ensure consistent brand identity in philanthropic efforts; directs preparation of all printed materials.

* Bachelor's Degree or equivalent education and experience required.
* Master's Degree (preferred).

jobs.title: Leland House Program Director
jobs.description:
**PRC Baker Places** is a non\-profit organization dedicated to serving the San Francisco community through legal advocacy, workforce development, financial services, and residential treatment programs. We support formerly homeless adults living with co\-occurring mental health and substance use disorders by providing a continuum of integrated direct care services. All of our programs are grounded in a social rehabilitation philosophy that integrates harm reduction and daily living skills within a safe and supportive environment.**Mission Statement:** Our mission is to help people affected by HIV/AIDS, substance use, or mental health issues better realize opportunities by providing integrated legal, social and health services that address the broad range of social risk factors that impact wellness and limit potential.

**Values that Guide Us:** Accountability, Honesty, Integrity, Diversity \& Inclusion, Respect


If you’re passionate about making a real impact in your community, working in a dynamic, inclusive environment, and helping people rebuild their lives, PRC Baker Places is the place for you.

jobs.title: COO MJHS Provider Organizations
jobs.description:

We offer a broad range of services in the community or facility\-based to help patients and their families ease the burden of managing a life\-limiting illness or end of life care.  

  

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) reports directly to the CEO, President and holds accountability to the Board for all Service Delivery operational matters. The COO will provide strategic and operational leadership across a continuum of post\-acute care services, including home care, hospice, and facility\-based long\-term care and skilled nursing. The COO will ensure the delivery of high\-quality, patient\-centered care while driving operational excellence, regulatory compliance, sustainable growth and profitability across all service lines and locations.

	+ Lead and collaborate with Service area\-heads to oversee operations across Home Care, Hospice, and Skilled Nursing facilities.
	+ Direct the achievement of organizational goals, including quality patient care, employee engagement, census growth, revenue, and net income through ongoing enhancement of internal operations and external service delivery processes.
	+ Drive innovation and standardize workflows and care protocols to ensure consistency, safety, and quality across all service settings.
	
	Oversee all resource allocation to meet patient needs efficiently in each service area.  
	+
* **Strategic Leadership**
	+ Collaborate with the CEO and executive team to develop and execute strategic plans for service expansion, geographic growth, and operational integration.
	+ Identify and implement opportunities for service line optimization and cross\-functional collaboration, with a view to reducing costs and maximizing revenue.
	
	Lead initiatives to enhance patient experience, reduce readmissions, and improve care transitions.  
	+

	+ Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations including CMS, DOH, and accreditation bodies (e.g., Joint Commission, etc.).
	+ Partner with clinical leadership to maintain high standards of care, infection control, and safety.
	+ Monitor and respond to changes in reimbursement models, including value\-based care and managed care contracts.

	+ In collaboration with the CFO, SVP of Information Systems and Chief Strategy Officer, drive adoption of appropriate health IT systems including EMRs, remote monitoring, and telehealth platforms.
	+ Support data\-driven decision\-making through performance analytics.
	+ Lead digital transformation initiatives to improve operational efficiency and patient engagement.
* **Leadership \& Culture**
	+ Capacity to lead organizational change and transformation.
	+ Ability to inspire through a balanced approach that combines authority, persuasion, dialogue, inspiration, analytical thinking, and experience.
	+ Develop and maintain strong working relationships with physicians and other health care professionals.
	+ Build and mentor a high\-performing operations leadership team across all service lines.
	+ Foster a culture of compassion, accountability, and continuous improvement.
	+ Promote interdisciplinary collaboration and staff development.
* Manages performance of direct and indirect reports. Provides orientation, coaching, training, and development. Take corrective action when necessary.
* Utilizes corporate services resources such as Human Resources, Compliance, Legal, Finance, Information Services, Marketing, etc., as appropriate.

Interviews and participates in the selection process for qualified staff in collaboration with Human Resources and department management.  
* 
* Master’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Nursing, or related field (MBA, MHA, MSN preferred).

* Experience with Medicare/NY Medicaid reimbursement and value\-based payment models in provider\-based programs.
* Familiarity with EMR systems.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer, Chicago Quantum Exchange
jobs.description:
**Department**


PME Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE) **About the Department**


The Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE) is an intellectual hub in the Midwest that connects leading universities, national labs, and industry partners to advance the science and engineering of quantum information, train the future quantum workforce, and drive the quantum economy. The CQE is based at the University of Chicago and anchored by the US Department of Energy’s Argonne National Laboratory and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, the University of Illinois Urbana\-Champaign, the University of Wisconsin–Madison, Northwestern University, and Purdue University. The community includes more than 50 corporate, international, nonprofit, and regional partners and is one of the largest collaborative teams working on quantum science in the world. The CQE leads national initiatives, including The Bloch Quantum Tech Hub, a US Economic Development Administration (EDA) designation endorsing the Chicago metro area as a central driver of US leadership in quantum technologies.  

  

The Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (UChicago PME) is the first school in the nation dedicated to molecular engineering, and integrates science and engineering to address global challenges from the molecular level up. UChicago PME’s rigorous academic and research programs are enhanced through the University of Chicago’s unique partnership with Argonne and Fermi National Laboratories, and the broad excellence of scholarship and education on campus. In the next phase of growth as a School, PME will continue to expand its team of world\-class faculty researchers and empower students from diverse backgrounds to collaborate with faculty in cutting\-edge facilities. PME aims to bring solutions for urgent societal problems to the forefront, while training the next generation of scientific leaders and entrepreneurs. **Job Summary**


The CEO of the Chicago Quantum Exchange develops and executes strategic plans to build a discovery\-to\-deployment research, innovation and commercialization, and talent ecosystem across the CQE member community, an external network of companies, non\-profits, and others. They will lead a team of skilled professionals and area managers to further CQE’s mission and vision, including the CQE’s Bloch Quantum EDA Tech Hub. Reporting to the CQE Faculty Director, this individual must be able to thrive in a fast\-moving, decentralized environment. The ideal candidate is a hands\-on leader able to set a vision to drive change internally; they have a can do, positive attitude, and are passionate about selling a strategic vision to key stakeholders including local and national leadership, faculty, and other internal and external partners.**Responsibilities**

* In alignment with the Faculty Director, designs, implements, and manages CQE’s overall growth strategy, furthering its mission, enabling its vision, and fostering novel quantum research, education and workforce development, and innovation and commercialization initiatives throughout the Quantum Prairie of Illinois, Indiana, and Wisconsin.
* Interacts with key stakeholders, internal leadership, external partners, and others to broker deals, continue to enhance CQE’s position and reputation, and grow CQE’s constellation of members and industry and other partnerships.
* Builds revenue\-generating programming, such as dues\-based memberships or partnerships and educational offerings, with an eye toward organizational sustainability.
* Understands the quantum marketplace and competitive dynamics and implications, including social and economic trends that impact CQE’s position and goals for growth and revenue.
* Enables advantageous positioning for CQE in consultation with leadership and key stakeholders to promote prominence in quantum\-related endeavors in the region.
* Pursues, through partnerships and direct reports, research collaborations, professional and other educational offerings and programs, and business development for the region.
* Through a diversified team of skilled professionals, drives awareness that aids in recruiting faculty, students, philanthropic and other sponsors, and industry partners.
* Establishes programs supported by federal and philanthropic funders, as well as the methodologies to measure, track and course\-correct.
* Builds a global profile for the CQE, and ensures the identity, voice, and objectives are articulated broadly to advantageous effect.
* Anticipates and solves a range of complex problems; work assignments are difficult and broad in nature, usually requiring creativity, originality, and ingenuity.
* Creates and implements data\-driven tools for measuring success and identifying opportunities for expansion in this emerging space.
* Provides strategic leadership for a Center with senior management and serves as a liaison to academic departments, professional organizations and administrative units of the University.
* Manages multiple related teams. Establishes department priorities, is responsible for the management of the center budget, allocates resources and executes strategic plans.
* Performs other related work as needed.

jobs.title: Founding Director of Operations
jobs.description:
**ROLE AT A GLANCE**


The Director of Operations is a Founding leadership role responsible for launching and scaling operations at Power Public Schools. Reporting to the Founder \& Executive Director, this role owns student recruitment and enrollment, facilities and campus operations, human resources and personnel administration, school logistics (transportation, safety, food service), student information systems and data compliance, and financial administration with internal controls. This is a mission\-critical role for our August 2027 launch and beyond as we build from one founding school toward a multi\-school network. Success requires an operator who can build systems others rely on, anticipate challenges, and navigate startup complexity with both urgency and equity\-centered judgment.

**Level:** Experienced — 3 to 5\+ years in operations, finance, or nonprofit management

**Type:** Full\-Time, 12\-Month, Exempt

**Location:** Mableton, Georgia (hybrid; on\-site upon opening of the school)

**Reports To:** Founder \& Executive Director

**Peers:** Founding Principal


**Mission:** Public Education / Charter School Launch

**Primary Tools:** Google Suite: Calendar, email, document; sheets; Zoom for video\-conferencing; Slack for Team Communication; Asana for task management; AI tools for drafting, summarizing, and building systems; cloud accounting, HR platforms, procurement systems

 **WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS**


Building a school from the ground up requires disciplined systems, thoughtful planning, regulatory readiness, and consistent execution. The Founding Director of Operations is the operational backbone of Power Public Schools, translating vision into the people, processes, partnerships, and infrastructure required for a safe, compliant, and successful opening day, and for every ordinary day after it.


You will lead the school's non\-instructional operations and coordinate the internal team members, external consultants, vendors, and service providers who execute this work. You remain accountable for operational readiness while partnering closely with the Founder and Executive Director, the external CFO, the HR consultant, board leadership, and specialized advisors.

 **COMPENSATION \& BENEFITS**

**﻿Salary:** $85,000–$95,000 base, commensurate with experience and demonstrated operational leadership.

**Benefits package includes** employer\-supported retirement, health, dental, fertility and vision coverage, paid time off per the employee handbook, tuition reimbursement, and professional development and operational coaching in partnership with external consultants and the Founding Leadership Cohort.

**﻿ABOUT POWER PUBLIC SCHOOLS**


Power Public Schools is a tuition\-free public charter school opening in August 2027 in Mableton, Georgia, in South Cobb County. We open with grades 6 and 7 and 100 students, and we grow deliberately from there. Slow growth is a choice. It lets us get every year right before we add the next one.


At Power Public Schools, we believe ALL people possess a power of intrinsic intelligence. Our mission is to excite, enlighten, and empower ALL our students to exemplify their excellence.


We teach through the POWER 5 Innovation Model (Premier Pedagogy; Power Principles; Power Learning AI; Power Hour \& Passion Projects; \& Practical Partnerships); the Georgia Standards of Excellence; AI\-empowered personalized mastery; project\-based community passion projects; early college and dual enrollment pathways; and leadership development. We are founder\-led, in the pre\-launch build phase, and we are building the operational, academic, and cultural foundation for a school meant to last generations.


We are an organization built on love. We ask every team member to hold the bar, own their growth, do hard things, lead with love, shine their light, and be the model.

**﻿**

**﻿WHAT YOU'LL OWN**


As Director of Operations, you will own the strategic design, implementation, and daily management of the operational infrastructure that enables Power Public Schools to function with excellence, equity, and reliability. You'll report to the Founder \& Executive Director and partner with school leadership to ensure every system—from student enrollment to facilities to finance—is documented, measurable, accountable, and continuously improving.

**1\. Founding\-Year Launch Management and Operational Readiness:** You will hold the integrated operational launch plan and make dependencies, deadlines, risks, and decisions visible across workstreams.

* Translate the opening vision into a sequenced, owner\-assigned launch plan with milestones, critical paths, decision dates, and contingency plans.
* Run a disciplined operating cadence: launch dashboards, weekly priority reviews, decision logs, risk registers, and clear follow\-through.

jobs.title: Development Director - Texas Bar Foundation
jobs.description:
General Description:

Reports directly to the Executive Director. Responsibilities to include cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of individual and corporate sponsorship support for the Texas Bar Foundation. Performs the duties of planning, organizing, directing, and coordinating special development efforts.  

Primary Functions:
* Works closely with the Fellows Chair, Development Committee, and seventeen district area chairs to develop and implement fundraising strategies, solicit and secure funds, cultivate existing donors, and acquire new donors. Responsible for training and recruiting materials.
* Trains, manages, and stewards volunteer solicitors. Assists in acquiring 200\+ volunteers in the 17 districts.
* Oversees the Development Committee and develops and manages endowment fundraising initiatives, including identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors and prospects to secure long\-term philanthropic support.
* Develops and oversees planned giving initiatives, including cultivating prospective legacy donors, coordinating planned gift outreach, and stewarding donors who have included the organization in their estate plans.
* Manages achievement award program: supports the selection committees, conducts oral history interviews, produces plaques and mementos, and writes the printed program and presentation scripts.
* Performs duties of planning, organizing, and implementing fundraising events and the annual dinner.
* Maintains accurate and detailed data regarding solicitation activities and creates tracking reports.
* Represents Bar Foundation in communications with donors, volunteers, Board members, and external stakeholders and provides a high level of customer service.
* Adheres to the budget and manages details for development\-related events, programs, fundraising initiatives, and vendor relationships.
* Assists with committee and Board meeting minutes and quarterly Board dinners and meetings and works with Board members to support development and fundraising initiatives.
* Responsible for updating donor information in Raisers Edge, and coordinates with Marketing and Communications Coordinator to produce and distribute memorial certificates, Life Fellow plaques, new Fellow certificates, and press releases. Directs and monitors vendors and mass mailings.
* Uses data strategically to produce accurate documents and reports. Requires proficiency in merge documents, database queries, and exports.
* Other duties as assigned.


Position Requirements:

The ideal candidate will have an entrepreneurial and strategic approach to fundraising. Bachelor’s degree plus three years of professional experience required, preferably in fundraising or membership development with a nonprofit organization. Supervisory experience preferred. Excellent interpersonal, written communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to take initiative and work independently and as part of a team. Experience and demonstrated success with annual giving, major donor programs, and/or individual and corporate solicitation preferred. Active membership in the Association of Fundraising Professionals (AFP) and/or other professional associations preferred. Knowledge of MS Word, Excel, and Access required; Raiser’s Edge preferred. Requires strong attention to detail, professionalism, and discretion. Position requires frequent overnight travel statewide.

The Executive Team provides enterprise\-wide leadership and strategic direction for Malala Fund. Working with the CEO, the team aligns priorities, resources, and action across functions and geographies. **POSITION OVERVIEW:**


The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a senior executive responsible for the strategic planning, development, implementation, and evaluation of the organization's programs. The COO ensures services align with the organization's mission and goals; deliver high\-quality, consistent, and impactful services; and remain responsive to the needs of consumers, families, funders, and the community. The COO leads organizational operations, clinical services, quality, compliance, and risk management.

Demonstrates behaviors aligned with the organization’s mission, values, and professional standards while supporting goals and initiatives through actions and attitude. jobs.title: Government & Political Affairs, Health & Payment Policy Director
jobs.description:
**Do you have a passion for shaping healthcare policy, advancing advocacy strategies, and building relationships that create a meaningful impact? Are you a strategic leader who combines expertise in government affairs and health policy with strong communication, collaboration, and organizational skills?**

**The American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) is seeking a Director of Government and Political Affairs, Health and Payment Policy to lead the development and implementation of the Society’s policy, advocacy, government relations, and private payer strategies. As a member of the senior management team, this individual will work closely with physician and staff leadership to identify and respond to emerging reimbursement, regulatory, patient safety, and legislative issues at the state and federal levels.**

**In this role, you’ll guide strategic communications with government agencies, private payers, healthcare organizations, and other key stakeholders while strengthening ASPS’s relationships with national, state, regional, and local partners. You’ll also collaborate with committees, task forces, volunteers, and staff leaders to advance programs that support public education, clinical practice, patient safety, research, and the overall mission of ASPS.**

**ABOUT US**


The American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) is the largest plastic surgery specialty organization in the world. Founded in 1931, the Society represents 92 percent of all board\-certified plastic surgeons in the United States, and more than 11,000 plastic surgeons worldwide – making ASPS a global institution and leading authority on cosmetic and reconstructive plastic surgery.


For more information about ASPS visit us at: https://www.plasticsurgery.org/


Follow us: Facebook I Instagram I Threads I X I TikTok I YouTube I LinkedIn

 **OVERVIEW**


Director, Government and Political Affairs, Health and Payment Policy

**Reports to:** COO, Executive Director of the Plastic Surgery Foundation

**Supervises:**


Sr. Government Affairs Associate \- Federal


Government Affairs Associate \- Federal

  

State Affairs Manager (Sr. Government Affairs Associate \- State)


Government Affairs Associate – Reimbursement


Health Policy Project Manager


Coding and Reimbursement Project Manager

**Location:** Remote in the US, Chicago or DC based preferred

**Travel:** approx 8x/year

 **WHAT YOU WILL DO**

* *Serve as a strategic advisor to ASPS/PSF physician and volunteer leaders, including the Board Vice President of Advocacy and Health Policy, the ASPS President, committees, task forces, and advisory groups.*
* *Lead and develop the Advocacy and Government Relations and Health and Payment Policy teams, ensuring high\-quality programs, resources, communications, and policy initiatives.*
* *Establish the strategic and financial direction of the departments, manage budgets, monitor revenue and expenses, and identify opportunities to generate non\-dues revenue and support organizational growth.*
* *Develop and execute state and federal advocacy strategies addressing legislative, regulatory, reimbursement, patient safety, and clinical\-practice priorities affecting plastic surgery.*
* *Serve as ASPS’s primary lobbyist before Congress, state legislatures, and other governmental and regulatory bodies while building relationships with key coalitions and partner organizations.*
* *Oversee ASPS’s engagement with public and private payers, advocating for appropriate coverage policies, reimbursement practices, and CPT valuation.*
* *Strengthen communication and engagement with ASPS members, physician leaders, state and regional plastic surgery societies, policymakers, payers, and other external stakeholders.*
* *Oversee PlastyPAC’s strategy and operations, including contribution planning, recipient assessment, and compliance with federal and state reporting requirements.*
* *Build advocacy capacity among ASPS members and affiliated societies through education, training, grassroots engagement, and state\-specific programs and resources.*
* *Represent ASPS and cultivate productive partnerships with organizations such as the AMA, CMSS, the Alliance for Specialty Medicine, medical associations, specialty societies, and other healthcare coalitions.*
* *Participate in evening conference calls and travel locally and out of state as needed,*

 **WHAT YOU WILL NEED**

* *A bachelor’s degree in public policy, business, communications, education, or a related field; an advanced degree is preferred.*
* *At least seven years of direct staff\-management experience, with a demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, and develop high\-performing teams.*
* *At least 10 years of experience in public policy, government affairs, advocacy, community mobilization, communications, or grassroots advocacy strategy.*
* *Proven success leading collaborative projects, developing advocacy initiatives, and planning and managing events.*
* *Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local government structures, legislative processes, regulatory activities, and advocacy strategies.*
* *Advanced policy and systems\-analysis capabilities, along with excellent managerial, budgeting, organizational, and prioritization skills.*
* *Exceptional written, verbal, interpersonal, and public\-speaking skills, with the ability to adapt communications for members, volunteer leaders, policymakers, and other stakeholders.*
* *The ability to work collaboratively with boards, committees, task forces, staff teams, and external partners.*

 **SALARY \& BENEFITS**

**Employment Type:** **Exempt**

**Annual Salary:** **$165,000 \- $175,000**

**Eligible for Overtime:** **No**

**Hours per Week:** **Full Time/37\.5 hrs per week**


The American Society of Plastic Surgeons offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes the following:

* Insurance: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, Disability, AD\&D, Critical Illness, Pet
* Pre\-Tax Spending Accounts: Health (HSA), Flexible (FSA), Child/Depende

jobs.title: Executive Director of Engagement and Annual Giving - Wharton External Affairs
jobs.description:
**University Overview**


The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world\-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News \& World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly\-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023\.


Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.


The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

**Posted Job Title**


Executive Director of Engagement and Annual Giving \- Wharton External Affairs**Job Profile Title**


Director E, Development, Fundraising**Job Description Summary**


Wharton School Overview  

Founded in 1881 as the world’s first collegiate business school, the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania is shaping the future of business by incubating ideas, driving insights, and creating leaders who change the world. With campuses in both Philadelphia and San Francisco, Wharton has over 850 staff, a faculty population of more than 235 renowned professors, and 5,000 undergraduate, MBA, executive MBA, and doctoral students. Each year 13,000 professionals from around the world advance their careers through Wharton Executive Education’s individual, company\-customized, and online programs. More than 104,000 Wharton alumni form a powerful global network of leaders who transform business every day. Wharton is home to a dynamic community of staff, bringing a wide range of skills, experiences, and perspectives. To learn more, visit www.wharton.upenn.edu.  

  

The Executive Director of Engagement and Annual Giving is a senior leader within Wharton External Affairs responsible for setting and executing a comprehensive, integrated strategy for communications, alumni engagement, and annual giving in support of the School’s philanthropic and engagement priorities. Reporting to the Sr Exec Dir of Development, this role provides strategic direction across Annual Giving, Alumni Relations, and Advancement Communications to strengthen donor engagement, deepen alumni connection, expand broad\-based participation, and grow annual fund revenue.
  

This position oversees teams responsible for strategic communications, alumni engagement, and annual fund initiatives, aligning messaging, outreach, and engagement opportunities across the full donor lifecycle, from identification and cultivation through solicitation and stewardship. The Executive Director partners closely with senior leaders across External Affairs, Wharton leadership, and Penn Development and Alumni Relations to ensure that communications, alumni engagement strategies, and annual giving efforts are coordinated, data\-informed, and effectively advance institutional priorities. The role requires a forward\-thinking, collaborative leader who can integrate functions, optimize performance, and build innovative programs that deepen alumni connection and expand philanthropic support.**Job Description**

**Job Responsibilities**

* Strategic leadership: Establish an integrated vision and operational framework across communications, alumni affairs, and annual fund that aligns messaging, engagement, and solicitation strategies to advance Wharton’s philanthropic priorities and strengthen alumni affinity..
* Integrated communications and engagement strategy: Oversee the development and execution of comprehensive, multi\-channel communications, alumni engagement programs, and annual giving campaigns that drive participation, enhance the donor experience, and elevate the School’s case for support.
* Senior Leader Collaboration: Collaborate with other senior leaders to develop and execute coordinated strategies that span the full donor life\-cycle and ensure alignment of goals, resources, and performance metrics
* Institutional partnership and alignment: Build and sustain strategic relationships with academic and administrative leadership, Wharton Marketing and Communications, and Penn Development and Alumni Relations to ensure consistency of messaging and effective integration of engagement and fundraising initiatives.
* Portfolio Ownership: Manage a focused portfolio of up to 25 leadership annual giving donors.
* Leadership \& People Management: Leads and supports direct reports through coaching, regular feedback, goal\-setting, and day\-to\-day guidance.
